title: The Boardroom USB
incident: A confidential M&A deck detailing a $500M hostile takeover appeared on an anonymous financial blog. The file was accessible to only 5 executives during an off-network strategy dinner in the boardroom. The host workstation shows no internet connection or standard email transmission.
centralQuestions: When was the acquisition presentation actually copied?
Was the leak transmitted via an unauthorized USB drive or a rogue Bluetooth pairing?
Who had access to the boardroom presentation computer prior to the meeting?

timeline.event: Executive Assistant prepares boardroom presentation laptop and preloads M&A slide deck.
Executive dinner commences; boardroom Faraday cage shielding activated.
Presentation delivered from laptop to boardroom projection screen.
Meeting ends; executives depart for airport.
Takeover deck screenshots posted by anonymous journalist on financial blog.

suspects.name: Evelyn Reed
suspects.motive: Shorting company stock through an offshore broker.
suspects.statement: She says she was presenting slides from the podium the entire dinner.
relevant_evidence: Her phone was left in the Faraday phone locker outside.
supporting_evidence: Board members confirm she stood at podium.
suspicious_evidence: Her smart wristwatch had local storage capability.
suspects.uncertainty: Smart watches inside the Faraday cage cannot broadcast to the internet.
open_questions: Did her watch connect via physical cable?

suspects.name: Julian Vance
suspects.motive: Passed over for partner promotion; received competitor recruitment offer.
suspects.statement: He claims he was sitting in the corner taking minutes on paper.
relevant_evidence: A stealth micro-SD card reader disguised as an executive fountain pen found in his pocket.
His badge was used to enter the boardroom at 5:15 PM.
suspicious_evidence: Was inside the boardroom 15 minutes before the assistant preloaded the laptop.
suspects.uncertainty: Being in the room before the file is loaded does not explain how the file was copied after it was preloaded.
open_questions: Did he install a persistent hardware sniffer?

suspects.name: Tara Cole
suspects.motive: Heavy credit card debt; brother works for rival financial publication.
suspects.statement: She says she downloaded the presentation from the secure intranet at 5:30 PM and left the room at 5:45 PM.
relevant_evidence: Only person who had the administrative password to unlock the presentation file.
supporting_evidence: Badge log shows her leaving 40th floor at 5:50 PM.
suspicious_evidence: The original presentation file in her sent folder was modified at 5:32 PM.
suspects.uncertainty: Modifying file properties is standard when converting PowerPoint to presentation kiosk mode.
open_questions: Did she copy the file before putting it on the presentation laptop?

witnesses.name: IT Director Hall
witnesses.statement: The boardroom laptop had physical USB ports disabled via Group Policy—a standard thumb drive will not mount.
witnesses.limitations: Does not apply to internal PCIe or hardware bus emulators.

evidence.title: Wireless Kiosk Mouse Receiver Log
evidence.description: The USB wireless mouse dongle plugged into the presentation laptop had a flash memory controller (HID attack device).
evidence.establishes: The mouse receiver contained an embedded 32GB storage chip capable of bypassing USB mass storage blocks.
evidence.does_not_establish: Who purchased or plugged in the mouse dongle.

evidence.title: Badge Ingress Log (5:15 PM)
evidence.description: Julian Vance badged into boardroom at 5:15 PM and replaced the standard wireless mouse with the modified unit.
evidence.establishes: Vance was alone in the room immediately prior to setup.

evidence.title: Blog Screenshot Metadata
evidence.description: PNG screenshots published at 10:15 PM contain EXIF camera data from an iPhone 14 Pro.
evidence.establishes: The leaked images were photographs of a screen, NOT digital file exports.

evidence.title: Cloud Staging Cache Timestamp
evidence.description: An unindexed temporary zip archive containing the merger dossier was generated at 11:15 AM, two hours before the board meeting.
evidence.establishes: The acquisition files were pre-packaged before any attendee entered the boardroom.
evidence.does_not_establish: Whose hands initiated the batch extraction script.

evidence.title: Hardware Hub Device Registry
evidence.description: Conference room table smart-dock logged a transient USB Mass Storage connect-disconnect sequence lasting 42 seconds.
evidence.establishes: A flash drive drew power during the executive recess.
evidence.does_not_establish: Which seat occupant plugged in the drive.
evidence.reliability_notes: Authenticated syslog from Cisco switch port.

redHerrings: The modified USB mouse dongle appeared to be the theft vehicle, but the leaked document was actually photo screenshots, meaning the digital USB attack failed or was unused.
Evelyn Reed's smartwatch had no camera capable of taking high-resolution 4K photos.

hiddenSolution.explanation: While setting up the presentation at 5:35 PM on the 40th floor (before the Faraday cage phone lockup was instituted at 6:00 PM), Tara Cole used her personal iPhone 14 Pro to take high-resolution photographs of the slides on the monitor, texted them to her journalist contact, and left at 5:50 PM.
decisiveEvidence: E-C (EXIF data proving photo of screen)
Timeline (Setup occurred before phone lockup at 6:00 PM)
uncertainties: Whether Julian Vance's USB dongle was an independent concurrent espionage attempt
hiddenSolution.alternativeExplanation: Julian Vance took the photos using his micro-camera pen during the presentation.

missingEvidence: Corridor camera footage of Tara Cole holding her phone at 5:35 PM
rules: Inspect the file format of the leak: a photograph of a screen disproves a digital file extraction theory.
Faraday cage restrictions only apply while active.
